label: late original-phase steps, weak conjunction of first token (d/y), previous input (w/o/t) and current input
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.04% of steps). 97% of activation mass falls in the original phase at t>=3 (never t<3); a little at the <DEL> step; essentially never in the copy phase. Within that window, firing is raised by several independent soft factors: first token d or y (11x and 7x lift), previous input w/o/t (12x, 7x, 4x), and current input in {w,0,b,a,g,x,r,u}. Lift grows with position (orig_idx 8 is 7.9x) and with L. No single factor or conjunction of them reaches useful precision: the best 3-way conjunction gets dev F1 0.13 (precision 0.07, recall 0.50). The pattern looks like an additive hidden-state direction rather than a crisp token rule. The largest activations come from sequences that start with d and have repeated w near the end of the original phase. Magnitude was not otherwise characterized.
